records.claim: Lithium passes into the breast milk. The amount of lithium that gets into a baby’s blood through breast milk is much less than the amount in the woman’s blood. If you take lithium while breastfeeding, monitor the baby for symptoms such as restlessness, low muscle tone, or trouble feeding. There are a few reports of reversible changes in a baby’s thyroid and kidney function, so it has been recommended to monitor the baby’s lithium level, thyroid function, and kidney function, especially in very young or preterm infants. If you suspect the baby has any symptoms, contact the child’s healthcare provider.
